description.narrative: Stöd för att utveckla ett integrerat ärendehanteringssystem för det albanska rättsväsendet som en direkt finansiering till Albaniens höga rättsliga råd som genomförandepartner.
Support to develop an integrated case management system for the Albanian Judiciary through a direct funding to the High Judicial Council of Albania as the implementing partner.

The goal of this proposed intervention is to ensure that all people who seek justice in the courts will be given so with transparency, efficiency, less costs and easily accessible. This goal is embedded in the HJC mission as cooperation partner to build, lead, and govern a highperforming judicial system that demands excellence and deserves the public trust, as defined in the legal framework in force as well as the HJC Strategic Plan. Therefore, the main objective of this has been stated as "Strengthen the rule of law through improving the information and technology instruments that guarantee, efficiency and quality of service delivery in order to increase public confidence in the justice system". This will be achieved through the development of a new Integrated Case Management and Information System that aims to reach to following specific objectives:
- Increase the efficiency of the courts
Digitization, replacement of manual and double data entry, standardization and simplification of courts procedures, opportunity to exchange data with other systems serving to the needs of the Judiciary (in particular the Human Resources Management System and the systems dealing with finance) will decrease workload as well as financial and human resources needed. All functionalities of new integrated CMIS lead towards reduction of the duration of court proceedings and accurate and realtime data to manage the judiciary, by boosting court efficiency internally but also in relation to the public.
-Increase the quality of judicial work, its results and of data produced
A new CMIS will provide usable and flexible tools for: a) the drafting and the publication of judicial decisions in digital manner b) for a proper management of the courts caseload and of their calendars by providing alerts on deadlines and informing the users about tasks or events in need of attention, as well as c) information on courts performance and judicial caseload trends, through the indepth analysis of CMIS data processed. By reducing the workload of court staff and automatisation of work processes, automatically we have created opportunities to increase the quality of their work and at the same time to increase the quality of services provided to citizens.
-Increase the transparency, accountability and inclusiveness
Electronic access and provision of electronic services to society, through enable the electronic filing of data and documents by external users, will increase the access of interest groups and citizens to the Albanian judicial system. Additionally, a new CMIS will offer the opportunity for different users to access judicial decisions via a onestopshop solution (e.g., ejustice portal) without having the need to follow the current procedure through request for information. By offering digital services though onestop approach will increase openness and transparency of the court. At the same time, it will offer the public and interest groups (media representatives, civil society actors, business communities, etc.) the necessary tools to better exercise their rights of inclusiveness and to keep institutions accountable. Establishment of a centralized, unified and integrated a new CMIS, which will replace the existing systems currently used in the Albanian judiciary, both suffering from numerous shortcoming as well as lack of functionalities required for further digitalization of manual paperbased processes, would significantly improve the efficiency of the courts, create better working conditions in line with current technological developments, increasing efficiency, transparency and accountability in the judicial system, as well as fulfilling legal obligations.

sector.narrative: Justice, law and order policy, planning and administration

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between Sweden and HJC for the ICCMS (14076)

description.narrative:
During the period January 2025- May 2026 the intervention established the necessary technological foundation for the development of the New Integrated Case Management System (JURONIX/ ICMIS) to operate. After a protracted procurement process of the company to develop the new case management system, the winning companies organized in a consortium were selected. One specializes in hardware and the other in software development. The finalization of the procurement process was delayed due to appeals to the Procurement Commissioner from one of the non-winning bidders. The contract was signed after clearance from the Albanian National Procurement Agency and the work started immediately after for the software development. The supporting hardware infrastructure for the new system was procured and delivered previously. The objectives of the initiation and analysis phases for the development of the ICCMS/JURONIX have been successfully fulfilled, along with the procurement of the software infrastructure. Main achievements include: - The procurement of the company that will develop the ICCMS/JURONIX - Completion of analytical visits to six representative courts of different levels and jurisdictions. As a result of the analysis, the key functionalities that the JURONIX system must provide to increase operational efficiency have been identified and documented - Conducting study visits to Swedish judicial institutions, enabling the identification of best practices for system design. During the study visit to Sweden, the team became acquainted with the VERA system of Domstolsverket and the way in which the Swedish national courts administration manages judicial cases electronically, providing each court level with direct access to the necessary data. The Swedish model - whereby the Court of Appeal accesses audio records of first instance hearings through a secure link - has been identified as a transferable best practice in the Albanian context -Establishment of two working groups (functional and legal), ensuring institutional inclusion and inter-institutional harmonization. The legal changes group will identify issues in connection to the development of the new system that would require legal changes either as laws, by laws or rules and procedures to be enacted -Collection and analysis of data through structured questionnaires for court administration and system users, and through site visit in courts of different levels and jurisdictions. Each visit had an in-depth analytical character, following the complete judicial workflow and documenting processes at every hierarchical level - from the judge to the judicial secretary, from the chief chancellor to the registration staff. During the visit to the Special Court of First Instance for Corruption and Organized Crime, the objective of guaranteeing full traceability and auditing of every action in the system was discussed, as well as the need for strict access control to audio recordings of hearings, matters of significant importance for institutional integrity - Completion of the initiation and analysis reports, which document in detail the existing processes and functional requirements of the system - Procurement, installation and functional verification of key IT infrastructure components, essential for the deployment of the system.
These achievements are of strategic importance, as they ensure that the future system is built upon real operational needs, reducing the risk of mismatch between system functionalities and judicial practice, as well as increasing the probability of a successful implementation. The analysis phase has also enabled the identification of the key shortcomings of the current system, such as manual processes, the lack of reliable statistics and limited inter-institutional interaction, all of which will be directly addressed by the new system.
The HJC has intensified its outreach to different groups of users of the system like the National Bar Association and the general public. During this period the intervention was launched publicly with broad participation from the different institutions and the media. The features required from the new system were presented through a documentary and drew high level of interest from the courts and other participants. The event served as public outreach activity and generated high expectations from the users, especially the courts, and commitment to continue the engagement with the developers and HJC.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
